- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.2) within 5 days, model overcorrects downward; adjust downward bias by +1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods; if sentiment is neutral or negative, forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) true values; increase forecast tail by 1–3% for final 10 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1,0,1,0), model exhibits lagged reaction; delay forecast peak by 1–3 days relative to sentiment peak.
